title: Grateful Dead Live at Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum on 1973-03-16
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> SEK'D Prodif Plus -> Samplitude Professional -> FLAC
source: Set 1: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat (44.1k) DSet 2: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (44.1k) D

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture with a crisp mix (though the board runs hot early) of a high‑energy 1973 Nassau show that smokes on Dark Star, Bird Song and a monster Playing in the Band.
ai_review.review: This Charlie Miller SBD delivers excellent mastering and clear soundstage, aside from occasional clipping caused by overly hot board levels in the first set. Musically the performance is quintessential ’73 – the band is tight, the energy is high and standout moments include Dark Star, Bird Song, the China→Rider sandwich with a Feelin’ Groovy jam, and a thunderous Playing in the Band/Truckin' → Morning Dew finale.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating ≈4.6★, with consistent praise for both performance and sound; only minor technical complaints (clipping) keep it from perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clean mastering typical of Miller releases; occasional hot board levels cause clipping in the first set but improve as the music quiets in the second set.

standout_songs: Playing in the Band > The Wheel > Truckin' > Morning Dew
show_quality.setlist_flow: Classic 1973 two‑set flow – a punchy first set with strong openers and a soaring closer, followed by a second set that builds from Promised Land into an expansive Dark Star and finishes with a powerful Truckin' → Morning Dew.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is praised as perfect; his soloing is described as “serious licks” that drive the jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass work repeatedly called a “smoke‑show,” with several reviewers noting he “bombs” and adds strong backing vocals.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocal performance gets positive nods (e.g., strong lead on ‘Looks Like Rain’), but no specific instrumental commentary.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano/keyboard contributions are highlighted as a showcase, adding mojo to jams and the second‑set transitions.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is praised for its intensity and “great drumming” throughout the show.
